Resolves #18945

🪢 *Give a grid column an `id`, and its header button took the same one: the instance manager logged a refusal on every boot, the DOM node with that id was the button, and the App Worker answered for it with the column.*

## What changes

`grid.Container#createColumns` builds a column's header button from the column's own config. It now drops `id` from that copy: the column keeps the id the app gave it, and the button takes a generated one, like the button of every column without an id.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium, CI-executed component tier) → L3 required (AC-1…AC-3). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the PR baseline jobs run in CI. Change class: restoration (`fix`).

Micro-review eligible: mechanical — one deleted config key plus one component arm.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: new `component/grid/ColumnId.spec.mjs` — reads the console itself, because `Neo.logError` raises nothing a `pageerror` gate sees. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: same arm — `Neo.worker.App.getConfigs({id})` answers `Neo.grid.column.Base` / `c3`, and no DOM node carries the id. |
| AC-3 | Outside CI: red on `dev`'s `Container.mjs` (`the button does not carry the column's id`), 5 of 5 green here. CI-covered: e2e `grid`, component `grid`, unit `grid`. |

Red-first against `dev`'s `src/grid/Container.mjs`: 1 of 1 red. No consumer in `src/grid`, `src/draggable/grid` or `src/selection/grid` reads a header button through its column's id.
